analysis.investment_thesis: Citichem fails the Magic Formula's critical Return on Capital test with an ROE of just 0.09%, indicating a commodity trading business with virtually no earning power on its capital base. The headline P/E of 4.96 is mathematically suspect at this ROE level and doesn't compensate for the absence of any business quality.
key_strengths: Optically low P/E of 4.96 (earnings yield proxy ~20%)
Promoter holding at 61.21% shows skin in the game
Debt-light trading model (implied by small balance sheet)
key_risks: ROE of 0.09% is effectively zero — catastrophic return on capital
Nano-cap at 8.87 Cr — illiquid, prone to manipulation
Chemical trading is a low-margin, no-moat commoditized business
red_flags: ROE 0.09% is incompatible with a genuine P/E of 4.96 — suggests one-off or distorted earnings
Market cap under 10 Cr — classic penny-stock territory
No evidence of sustainable EBIT or ROIC trend
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Magic Formula standpoint, this stock is a hard pass. The two variables I care about are Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) and Return on Capital (EBIT/(NWC+NFA)). While the P/E of 4.96 suggests a superficially attractive earnings yield, an ROE of 0.09% tells me the business is generating essentially nothing on the capital deployed — that's deep below my 20%+ ROIC threshold and even below the 12% minimum I'd tolerate. Chemical trading is a spread business with thin margins and no structural moat; Citichem has been around since 1992 without compounding into anything meaningful, which itself is evidence of poor capital returns.

The P/E vs ROE mismatch is also a red flag — it usually means either a one-time gain is inflating trailing earnings or the equity base is distorted. At an 8.87 Cr market cap, this is a nano-cap where liquidity and governance risk dominate any fundamental thesis. The Magic Formula explicitly seeks "cheap AND good" — Citichem is arguably cheap on one optical metric but decisively not good. Skip it and wait for a name that clears both filters.
